extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for HFSP Research Grants or HFSP Postdoctoral Fellowships (interdisciplinary life-science teams and postdocs seeking cross-disciplinary training)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and guidance for HFSP Research Grants (interdisciplinary international team projects) and HFSP Postdoctoral Fellowships (cross-disciplinary postdoctoral training). Covers core review dimensions, discouraged patterns, scoring mechanism, and fellowship-specific discipline-change requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty / scientific quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research must extend the frontiers of knowledge; must NOT be obvious next-step work from the applicant's lab; must NOT continue ongoing collaborations among the team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HFSP looks for work that is frontier-pushing rather than incremental. Avoid proposing projects that are obvious continuations of the applicants' current lab work or that largely continue existing collaborations. Emphasize conceptual advance, originality, and how the project departs from prior directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Team members must come from genuinely different disciplines; crossing biological/physical/computational boundaries is favored; mere multi-disciplinary collaboration is insufficient — true integration required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate genuine integration of different disciplinary perspectives and methods (not just co-location of disciplines). Explain how disciplinary expertise will be combined to create novel approaches or insights. Simple collaboration among disciplines without integration will be scored poorly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Synergistic collaboration plan with distinct contributions from each PI; geographic diversity (cross-country teams favored); track record of team members in their respective fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear plan showing synergy and distinct, complementary roles for each investigator. Highlight how collaboration will be coordinated across countries and institutions and provide evidence (track records) that each PI can deliver their intended contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly discouraged proposal patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that are 'obvious next steps' in the applicants' labs; proposals where the team has previously published together; proposals that don't represent significant change in research direction; single-discipline proposals dressed up as interdisciplinary; established collaborations seeking continuation funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting incremental extensions, continuations of established collaborations, or rebranded single-discipline projects. If prior collaboration exists, explicitly explain how the new proposal is a substantive departure. Failure to address these points risks strong negative assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of the applicant (Postdoctoral Fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accomplishments relative to career stage; publication record (quality over quantity); letters of recommendation; demonstrated potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fellows, reviewers evaluate accomplishments appropriate to career stage, with emphasis on the quality and significance of outputs rather than sheer number. Strong, specific letters that address prospective development and independence are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of the proposed research (Postdoctoral Fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training potential (must teach the applicant new techniques/concepts); scientific originality; innovative character; clear departure from previous research (cross-disciplinary move required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship proposals must show that the postdoc will gain new skills and undergo a genuine discipline-change. Emphasize how the proposed research is original and innovative, and why it represents a clear move away from the applicant's PhD research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of the host laboratory (Postdoctoral Fellowships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of host PI; infrastructure and resources available; supervisor's track record with prior fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document host PI qualifications, available infrastructure and specific resources, and evidence of successful supervision/training of previous fellows. Show how the host environment will enable the applicant's cross-disciplinary training and research goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring mechanism and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Two committee members initially review each application; alphabetical scores A (highest), B, C, D (lowest); a third reviewer evaluates if scores differ significantly between the first two; final ranking based on aggregated reviewer scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the two-reviewer initial cut and the use of A–D categorical scoring. If reviews diverge, a third assessment may be requested. Applications should be crafted to achieve high categorical evaluations across reviewers (clarity on novelty, interdisciplinarity, and team strength).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-boundary (discipline-change) requirement for fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: For HFSP postdoc fellowships, the applicant's PhD must be in a clearly different discipline than the proposed postdoctoral work — this 'discipline change' is itself a scoring criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly document and justify the discipline change (e.g., bench-to-computational, physicist-to-biologist). Explain what new techniques/concepts will be learned and how the move constitutes meaningful cross-disciplinary training; failure to show a clear discipline change will weaken the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: HFSP penalizes continuity; rewards departure/novel direction
rubrics_metrics.description: HFSP's rubric actively penalizes continuity (with prior work, prior collaborators, prior discipline). Most agencies reward continuity as evidence of feasibility; HFSP treats it as evidence of insufficient novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should design proposals to emphasize departure from prior work and collaborations. Where continuity exists, explicitly articulate how the new project differs substantively. Use the proposal to demonstrate novelty, not just feasibility by prior track record.
